reading: Depth separates on this workflow: the baseline range (0.375 to 0.500) and the council range (0.875 to 1.000) are disjoint at n=3. This is the only workflow in the development grid where the ranges do not overlap.

controls.title: Validation exception queue at capture
controls.quote: Anything below the confidence threshold is not silently passed forward — it is routed to an AP-clerk exception queue with the specific low-confidence fields flagged, not the whole document.

controls.title: Variance packet assembled before handoff
controls.quote: when a match falls outside tolerance, the same agent assembles the variance packet (PO, GRN, invoice, computed variance, historical vendor pattern) before handing off, rather than dropping a bare "exception" flag

controls.title: Structured attributable resolution record
controls.quote: resolution rationale (VIP-04) and reconciliation sign-off (VIP-08) must be captured as structured, attributable records, not narrative comments buried in a ticket system

controls.title: Risk-tiered approval replacing uniform routing
controls.quote: Today's step implies uniform hierarchical routing for everything matched. I want…

controls.title: Auto-authorisation rule-fired log
controls.quote: my round-1 description of T-4 ("Risk-tiered approval and authorisation") specified that auto-approval events log "which rule authorised it," but I did not specify what the…

controls.title: Mandatory sampling audit of the auto-approved population
controls.quote: neither position has specified what fraction of volume is an acceptable delegation ceiling, nor what compensating control (sampling audits of auto-approved invoices? periodic re-authorisation of the delegation matrix itself?) prevents the delegated tier from silently…

controls.title: Governed delegation-of-authority policy engine for the low-risk tier
controls.marker: policy-delegation engine for the low-risk tier
controls.quote: I accept that a governed, versioned tolerance-rule and delegation-matrix object is the right mechanism for risk-tiering

controls.title: Offline-cached delegation policy with named fallback approver
controls.quote: I now accept that my tiered-approval design needs an explicit, auditable delegated/offline fallback authority (not a bypass, a named alternate approver with logged after-the-fact reconciliation)

controls.title: Matching kept as a discrete auditable step boundary
controls.quote: This remains a discrete step boundary, not an inline computation inside a larger pipeline, because the boundary is the auditable point at which the in…

controls.title: Discrete subledger lock preserved under continuous reconciliation
controls.quote: the period-end confirmed balance and the subledger lock that enforces cutoff (KB-03) must remain a hard gate — this is not something continuous reconciliation should be allowed to soften

reviewer_questions: The delegated approval tier has no stated volume ceiling. What fraction of invoice value may be auto-authorised before the sampling audit stops being a sufficient compensating control?

Segregation is specified at credential level between approval and posting. Is a service account executing delegated authorisation a distinct actor for VIP-R-06 purposes, or does the gate's actor comparison need to see identity rather than role name?
The offline approval fallback reconciles after the fact. What is the acceptable reconciliation window before an unreconciled offline approval becomes an audit finding?

excluded_claims.title: Segregation enforced at credential level
excluded_claims.reason: Excluded from the controls list: baseline draw 7fc2 already states "Authorisation is performed by an approver, structurally distinct from the accountant who later posts the entry." The council version is stronger (separate credentials, logs and escalation ownership, enforced architecturally) but the control is not absent from every baseline draw, so it is not claimed as council-only.
